messages.author: 828d260a55f62325
messages.subject: Variances in SPDE
parts:
Dear list

A quick general question about  SPDE models  just to double-check Im not missing the point! are the variances of the finite-element representation of the Matern field the same (or just nearly the same) for all individuals/locations as it is usually assumed in traditional geostatistics?

Thanks

Karim

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Variances in SPDE
parts:
Hi Karim,
They are approximately the same "away from the boundaries".  Near the boundaries, the variance is approximately twice the "stationary" variance.  This is a common feature of GMRF models and the typical approach is to extend the boundary far enough beyond the area of interest that the variances are approximately equal.

Best wishes,

Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Variances in SPDE
parts:
On 13/02/13 15:28, Karim Anaya wrote:
> A quick general question about SPDE models just to double-check Im
> not missing the point! are the variances of the finite-element
> representation of the Matern field the same (or just nearly the same)
> for all individuals/locations as it is usually assumed in traditional
> geostatistics?

At a distance of at least 1-2 times the correlation range away from the
boundary, yes, then they are approximately the same. Closer to the
boundary the variances are inflated by a factor 2-4, typically
(depending on the domain geometry). A more precise relation is given in
the 1D interval domain case in the Lindgren et al 2011 JRSSB SPDE/GMRF
paper, Appendix A I believe; For rectangular domains, a similar
expression holds, based on reflection in the domain edges.

The above of course only holds for the stationary SPDE operator case.
By letting the parameters depend on location one can for example
practically eliminate the boundary effect on the variance; this is
however not yet implemented in R-INLA.

Finn
